title: PRD: Hosted Inference Surface — Guardrails, Acceptance Matrix & Tiered Canary Scripts
creator: Ava Mitchell
description: Purpose: Define the product requirements, behavioral guardrails, acceptance matrix and scripted rollout for the unified hosted inference surface covering chat, completion, embeddings and rerank endpoints. Outcome: a testable PRD that enables engineering to implement API contracts, console controls for tiered canary traffic, operational runbooks, and a measurable launch checklist with SLOs and regression gates.
background: Redwood currently exposes multiple historical endpoints with overlapping semantics. Customers need a single predictable hosted surface that: 1) preserves behavioral contracts for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank, 2) provides deterministic fallback modes for degraded capacity, and 3) supports staged rollouts with traffic gating and measurable acceptance checks. This PRD consolidates feature-level requirements, non-functional expectations, rollout scripts, and migration guidance for customers and internal teams.
scope: Included: new unified endpoint surface (one route configurable for mode: chat|completion|embeddings|rerank)
Included: behavioral guardrails per-mode (response length/clamping, stop-token enforcement, embedding dimensionality validation, rerank score range enforcement)
Included: canary and tiered traffic gating in Console + API flags for deterministic rollout (0%, 1%, 5%, 25%, 100%)
Included: acceptance test suite (automated functional + perf + quality evals) and rollout scripts
Included: operational runbooks (rollback, fallback to compatible model variant, degraded-mode SLOs)
Excluded: changes to private/on-prem control plane wiring (separate PRD)
Excluded: introducing new token metering units or pricing tiers as part of launch
requirements: API: single hosted route /v1/inference with required 'mode' query or header indicating chat|completion|embeddings|rerank
API: explicit model versioning header (X-Model-Version) and behavior-preserving aliasing for historical endpoints
SDK: support for streaming + function/tool-calls across modes with consistent event framing
Console: per-route toggle for canary percentages, roll forward/rollback, and per-canary health indicators
Behavior: deterministic fallback chain when model variant is unavailable (primary -> quantized -> smaller model) with preserved token semantics
Observability: token-level cost, per-request latency, model-variant tag, and behavior regression score for a canary testset
Security: KMS integration for model keys and audit logging of model-selection and rollout changes
nonfunctional_requirements: Latency: 95th percentile generation latency < 300ms for short-completion profile (<=64 tokens) on Dedicated tier
Throughput: sustain 1000 rps aggregated across models in a pool for initial Dedicated-onboarding customers
Availability: Hosted API availability SLA target 99.95% during business-hours for GA lanes
Quality: canary-to-control semantic divergence score <= 2% on the canonical prompt suite for GA gates
Cost: supporting quantized fallbacks without increasing peak customer token cost by >5% for default routing
acceptance_criteria: API contract: verified schema with contract tests (negative and positive) for all four modes; public SDKs updated and unit-tested
Behavioral parity: run canonical prompt suite (500 prompts across categories) and ensure generation, stop token behavior and function-calling work within defined tolerance
Embeddings: vector dimensionality and normalization preserved for existing customers; cosine similarity drift < 0.02 against baseline embeddings
Rerank: score distribution sanity checks pass (scores in expected range, ordering preserved for canonical queries), A/B rerank precision delta < 1.5%
Operational: Console canary UI toggles operate end-to-end with correct traffic routing; engineers can scriptedly set canary to any supported percentage
Monitoring: dashboards show per-canary health, top 10 error classes, and drift indicator; alerts configured for regression and latency SLO breaches
Rollout script: one-button canary progression script completes staging->1%->5%->25%->100% with gates preventing progression on failing checks
Security: KMS audit events for rollout changes recorded and accessible; SSO/SAML gating for rollout permission verified
Docs: PRD-linked public developer docs and migration guide published; quickstart examples for each mode in SDKs
metrics_and_gates: Functional gates: end-to-end request success rate >= 99.5% for each canary stage
Quality gates: semantic divergence on canonical prompt suite <= 2% (fail fast)
SLO gates: P99 latency must not increase by >20% from baseline during canary
Infra gates: error budget burn during canary <= 1% of allowed budget for the cycle
Manual gate: Product sign-off required before 25% and 100% traffic steps
rollout_checklist: 1. Preflight: run full integration CI including SDKs, contract tests, and eval harness
2. Staging deploy: end-to-end smoke tests, ingest telemetry into staging dashboards
3. Canary 1%: run canary suite for 24 hours; monitor functional/quality/latency gates
4. Canary 5%: run canary suite for 48 hours and run extended evals for embeddings/rerank stability
5. Canary 25%: run for 72 hours with enterprise traffic shape tests and autoscaling observations
6. GA 100%: complete migration plan for customers on legacy endpoints and enable migration toggle in Console
7. Post-GA: 30-day regression monitoring and weekly quality reviews; bug triage and hotfix runbook prepared
monitoring_and_observability: Dashboards: per-route latency (p50/p95/p99), error rate, token consumption, model-variant distribution
Quality telemetry: semantic divergence score, per-prompt category failure rate, embedding similarity drift
Alerts: burst error rate > 0.5% for 5m, P99 latency breach triggers page, canary divergence > threshold triggers paging
Tracing: end-to-end trace id propagation from SDK to runtime and model execution layer
Audit logs: rollout changes, console toggles, and model selection events persisted for 90 days
migration_plan: Provide 'compat' mode on unified endpoint to emulate legacy behavior for a configurable period
Automatic redirect tool in Console to help customers move to new route with a preview of their traffic profile
Customer communication: staged emails and dashboard banners with migration timeline and opt-out instructions
Backwards compatibility: maintain legacy endpoints as aliases for 90 days post-GA before sunset with a deprecation schedule
runbooks_and_playbooks: Rollback playbook: steps to rollback canary or full deployment and re-route traffic to previous model-variant; includes DB migration rollback steps if any
Degraded-mode playbook: enable quantized fallback variant, notify downstream SLO owners, and raise incident with Runtime team
Hotfix release playbook: emergency branch cut policy, two-engineer approval for hotfix, postmortem template
risks_and_mitigation: Quality regression risk: mitigate with multi-signal eval harness and small seeded canaries before open traffic
Cost spike risk: track token-level cost and autoscaler interactions; set cost circuit breakers per-tenant
Behavioral drift for embeddings/rerank: keep baseline model variants for high-value customers and offer pinning
Permission drift: restrict rollout toggles to SSO groups and require two-person approval for GA step
decisions: Decision: single unified route chosen to simplify SDK surface and enable centralized telemetry
Decision: model-version header required to enable reproducible behavior and easier rollback
Decision: initial canary progression steps fixed at 1%, 5%, 25% to balance safety and speed

Product will own sign-off gates; Engineering owns execution and runbook accuracy
